body:
The context-menu catalog resolves lazy labels synchronously against every document Fluent resource marked optional. A missing message can make L10nRegistry enumerate resource/source combinations until the browser main process exhausts memory.

Search one candidate resource at a time alongside the two shared branding resources, using required resource semantics. This bounds each search while retaining native labels, translated lazy labels, plural arguments, and the existing label cache. Add a real-Fluent regression with the full browser resource list, a missing key, and a subsequent valid label.

Validation:

- Windows Floorp 12.20.0 / Gecko 157.0.1, Japanese locale and language pack, isolated profiles with a 2 GiB job limit: the original catalog hit the memory limit; the changed catalog completed the same missing-key lookup plus translated reload/plural labels in about 5 ms, with approximately 1 GiB peak browser memory.
- All 70 contextMenuRuntime.test.ts cases passed in the installed browser through Marionette with the changed TypeScript bundled for the test.
- Deno type checks, lint, formatting checks, and git diff --check passed.

Related: #2879, #2880. A local OOM dump reached Localization.formatMessagesSync, but its original missing key was not retained, so this PR does not automatically close those reports.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Context menu catalog labels now remain available when a translation is missing, while other available translations continue to display.
  - Missing translations no longer prevent later labels from being translated, and catalog capture leaves the native browser popup unchanged.

title: fix(context-menu): prevent memory runaway on missing Fluent labels
